extras-01-sdxl-batch.name: SDXL Batch
extras-01-sdxl-batch.description: SDXL with an upscale pass and a face pass. The prompt is built from four parts.

presets.label: Full
presets.note: Upscale and face pass, as built.

extras-01-klein-nsfw.name: Klein NSFW
extras-01-klein-nsfw.description: Text to image on a Flux.2 Klein finetune. One sampler pass, sized from an aspect ratio rather than raw pixels.

example.prompt: A woman standing at the rail of a ferry in late afternoon light, wind in her hair, the coastline out of focus behind her.

extras-01-realism-converter.name: Realism Converter
extras-01-realism-converter.description: Turns an existing picture photographic in two passes: Flux.2 Klein rebuilds it, then Z-Image Turbo refines at low denoise. Grain and contrast are applied last.

style.label: Style
style.note: This page was tuned against Photography | Fine Art. The list used to be 26 entries and did not contain it, so it opened on whatever was first - it is 320 now and the right one is there.

working_size.label: Working width
working_size.note: The Klein pass runs here. 2000 is the tuned size; smaller loses the texture the whole page exists to add.

cfg.label: CFG Scale
cfg.note: 1 is correct - Klein is distilled and does not want guidance.

refine_denoise.label: Refine denoise
refine_denoise.note: The Z-Image pass over the Klein result. 0.2 tightens skin and texture without moving anything; past about 0.35 it starts redrawing faces.

grain.label: Film grain
grain.note: Sensor noise. 0.02 is barely there and doing most of the work: a render is too clean, and a photograph never is. 0 looks synthetic again; past 0.05 it looks like a bad scan.

contrast.label: Contrast
contrast.note: 1.12 - a lift, not a look. AI output sits flat in the midtones and this is what stops it reading as a render.

refine_shift.label: Refine shift
refine_shift.note: How hard the refine pass bites. 3 is the tuned value - higher pushes texture further and starts inventing it.

example.prompt: photographic, natural skin texture, available light

extras-01-inpaint-pro.name: Inpaint Pro
extras-01-inpaint-pro.description: Repaints part of a picture and finds the part itself. The mask is matted, grown and softened before it is used, and a ControlNet holds the result to the shape of what was there.

mask_clothes.label: Mask clothes
mask_clothes.note: The mask to start from. Turning on face, hair and body as well selects the whole person, which is a mask that cannot land right because it is not aimed at anything.

mask_grow.label: Grow mask (px)
mask_grow.note: Pixels added around the mask. 50 reaches well past whatever was selected; 10 to 15 is usually enough to cover an edge.

mask_softness.label: Soften mask (px)
mask_softness.note: How far the edge fades. Keep it near mask_grow.

guidance_strength.label: Hold to original
guidance_strength.note: The ControlNet's hold on the original. Lower it if the result keeps coming back unchanged; 0 turns it off.

cfg.label: CFG Scale
cfg.note: realism-sdxl is a plain SDXL - its own header says epsilon - so it needs 5 to 8. At 1 the prompt barely reaches the sampler, which is what 'it changes too little' looks like.

denoise.label: Denoise
denoise.note: 1 is right here - the mask already decides what is repainted.

sampler.label: Sampler
sampler.note: dpmpp_2m for this checkpoint. lcm is for a distilled model, and on a normal SDXL it washes the result out.

example.prompt: bare skin, the light and shadow of the original photograph

extras-01-wan22-txt2vid.name: Wan 2.2 Text to Video
extras-01-wan22-txt2vid.description: A clip from a prompt on Wan 2.2 14B. Two passes - high noise then low - at four steps each, through an uncensored text encoder. Frames are doubled after sampling, so the clip is smooth at the same speed - set Smoothing to 1 to turn that off, and halve Frames per second if you do.

length.label: Length (seconds)
length.note: Wan 2.2 generates about five seconds of motion. Asking for more makes a longer file, not a longer performance - the clip runs out of motion and repeats. To go further, use the last frame this saves beside the video as the start image for Image to Video, and join the pieces.

example.prompt: a woman walks along a harbour at dusk, coat moving in the wind

extras-01-wan22-img2vid.name: Wan 2.2 Image to Video
extras-01-wan22-img2vid.description: Animates a picture you supply. Upload a frame that already shows everything the action needs - if the act happens below the crop, Wan tilts down to find it, and the body it invents down there is not hers. That single move is what most identity drift here actually is. Two passes on Wan 2.2 14B at four steps each, through an uncensored text encoder. Frames are doubled after sampling, so the clip is smooth at the same speed - set Smoothing to 1 to turn that off, and halve Frames per second if you do.

length.label: Length (seconds)
length.note: Wan 2.2 generates about five seconds of motion. Asking for more makes a longer file, not a longer performance - the clip runs out of motion and repeats. To go further, use the last frame this saves beside the video as the start image for Image to Video, and join the pieces.

example.prompt: she turns her head towards the camera and smiles, then holds the look

extras-01-wan22-flf2vid.name: Wan 2.2 First to Last Frame
extras-01-wan22-flf2vid.description: A clip that starts on one picture and ends on another. Wan 2.2 14B fills what happens in between. Frames are doubled after sampling, so the clip is smooth at the same speed - set Smoothing to 1 to turn that off, and halve Frames per second if you do.

length.label: Frames
length.note: Wan 2.2 generates about five seconds - roughly 81 frames at 16 fps. Past that the clip repeats rather than continuing. Chain from the last frame this saves beside the video to go further.

example.prompt: she lowers her head slowly, the light warming as she does

extras-01-klein-nsfw-img2img.name: Klein NSFW - Redraw
extras-01-klein-nsfw-img2img.description: Redraw a picture you already have on the Flux.2 Klein finetune. The upload keeps its own shape; denoise decides how much of it survives.

steps.label: Steps
steps.note: Denoise trims the schedule, so these are not all spent: at 0.7 a 24-step setting samples 17. Below about 16 there is no middle to find.

megapixels.label: Size (megapixels)
megapixels.note: The upload keeps its own shape; this is only how many pixels it is given.

denoise.label: How much to change
denoise.note: 0.5 keeps the picture, 0.7 keeps the pose and framing, 0.9 keeps only the composition. If 0.7 leaves the clothes on, raise steps before raising this.

example.prompt: A woman standing at the rail of a ferry in late afternoon light, wind in her hair, the coastline out of focus behind her.

extras-01-kontext-edit.name: Kontext Edit
extras-01-kontext-edit.description: Change a picture by describing the change. FLUX Kontext conditions on the image instead of repainting a hole in it, so the face, the pose and the light stay put.

prompt.label: What to change
prompt.note: An instruction, not a description of the whole picture: 'take the jacket off', 'make it night'. Everything you do not mention is meant to stay.

guidance.label: How literally to take it
guidance.note: 2.5 is the usual. Higher follows the words harder and drifts further from the picture; lower barely changes anything.

example.prompt: make it night, lit only by the window

extras-01-wan22-i2v-kiss.name: Wan 2.2 Kiss
extras-01-wan22-i2v-kiss.description: Animates a picture you supply into the two of them kissing. Same graph and same two-pass Wan 2.2 setup as Image to Video, with this act's LoRA pair already on. Upload a frame that already shows what the act needs - if it happens below the crop, Wan tilts down to find it and the body it invents there is not hers.

length.label: Length (seconds)
length.note: Wan 2.2 generates about five seconds of motion. Asking for more makes a longer file, not a longer performance - the clip runs out of motion and repeats. To go further, use the last frame this saves beside the video as the start image for Image to Video, and join the pieces.

example.prompt: she turns her head towards the camera and smiles, then holds the look
